t.1.70.3: The ten sons of Pracetas, all risen in splendour and equal in brilliance to the great seers, are remembered as virtuous men of former times; those mighty ones were once burned up by a fire born from the clouds.
t.1.70.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Now, in the lineage of the Prajāpati Dakṣa, of Manu Vaivasvata, and of Bharata, Kuru, Pūru and Ajamīḍha…
t.1.70.4: From them was born Dakṣa Prācetasa, and from Dakṣa these creatures came into being, O tiger among men; for he is the grandsire of the worlds.
t.1.70.2: O sinless one, I shall recount to you this lineage of the Yādavas, of the Pauravas in full, and likewise of the Bhāratas, a holy and great source of blessing that brings wealth, fame and long life.
t.1.70.5: Having united with Vīriṇī, the sage Dakṣa Prācetasa begot a thousand sons equal to himself, firm in their vows.
t.1.70.6: Nārada taught the assembled sons of Dakṣa, numbering a thousand, liberation and the unsurpassed knowledge of Sāṃkhya.
t.1.70.7: Then, O Janamejaya, Dakṣa the Prajāpati, wishing to create offspring, appointed fifty maidens as his putrikā daughters, whose sons would be counted as his own.
t.1.70.9: Of the thirteen wives, she who was the foremost daughter of Dakṣa, in her Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, begot the Ādityas, Indra and the others, endowed with valor, and also Vivasvant.
t.1.70.8: He gave ten to Dharma and thirteen to Kaśyapa, and to Indu he gave twenty-seven, who are engaged in the guiding of time.
t.1.70.11: To Mārtaṇḍa was born a son, the wise and mighty Manu. From Manu this lineage of men, the Mānavas, became renowned; from that Manu were born the Mānavas, the brahmins, kṣatriyas and the rest.
t.1.70.10: From Vivasvat a son was born, the lord Yama Vaivasvata; and to Yama also, O king, a son was born, Mārtaṇḍa.
t.1.70.12: There, at that time, O king, the brahman became united with the kṣatra. The brāhmaṇas among them, the descendants of Manu, preserved the Veda together with its limbs.
t.1.70.13: Vena, Dhṛṣṇu, Nariṣyanta, Nābhāga and Ikṣvāku, then Karūṣa and Śaryāti, and likewise here, as the eighth, Ilā.
t.1.70.14: They speak of the mighty sons of Manu, devoted to the duty of kṣatriyas, with Pṛṣadhra as the ninth and Nābhāgāriṣṭa as the tenth.
t.1.70.16: Then the learned Purūravas was born of Ilā. She was both his mother and his father, so we have heard.
t.1.70.15: Likewise, fifty other sons of Manu were born on earth; all of them perished through strife among themselves, so we have heard.
t.1.70.18: Purūravas, maddened by his own valor, made war upon the brahmins, and he seized the jewels of the brahmins even as they cried out in protest.
t.1.70.17: The greatly renowned Purūravas, though he was a man, enjoyed thirteen islands of the ocean, surrounded by beings who were not human.
t.1.70.19: Sanatkumāra, O king, came to him from the world of Brahmā and then admonished him, but he did not accept the counsel.
t.1.70.20: Then, cursed by the enraged great seers, the king, possessed by greed and bereft of his senses through the force of his intoxication, perished at once.
t.1.70.21: For he, the resplendent one, while dwelling in the world of the Gandharvas together with Urvaśī, brought down the fires for the performance of rites, duly arranged in a threefold manner.
t.1.70.22: Then six sons were born of Aila: Āyus, Dhīmant, Amāvasu, Dṛḍhāyu, Vanāyu and Śrutāyu, the sons of Urvaśī.
t.1.70.24: Nahuṣa, the son of Āyus, wise and of true valor, a lord of the earth, ruled a very great kingdom righteously.
t.1.70.23: Nahuṣa, Vṛddhaśarman, Raji, and the sinless Rambha: these, the sons of Svarbhānavī, are declared to be the sons of Āyu.
t.1.70.25: Nahuṣa protected the ancestors, the gods, the seers, the brahmins, the Gandharvas, the serpents and the Rākṣasas, as well as the brahmins and kṣatriyas, and the common people too.
t.1.70.26: Having slain the hordes of Dasyus, he made the seers pay tribute, and that mighty one made them carry him on their backs like beasts.
t.1.70.27: Having overpowered the dwellers of heaven by his splendor and his austerity, and likewise by his valor and his might, he exercised the sovereignty of Indra.
t.1.70.29: Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, was an emperor of true valor. He protected the earth and offered sacrifice with various soma-rites.
t.1.70.28: Nahuṣa begot six sons on Priyavāsā: Yati, Yayāti, Saṃyāti, Āyāti, Pāñca and Uddhava.
t.1.70.30: Ever self-restrained, honoring the ancestors and the gods with surpassing devotion, the unconquered Yayāti showed favor to all his subjects.
t.1.70.31: To him, O great king, were born of Devayānī and Śarmiṣṭhā sons who were mighty archers, endowed with every virtue.
t.1.70.32: Of Devayānī were born Yadu and Turvasu, and of Śarmiṣṭhā were born Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru.
t.1.70.33: O king, while that son of Nahuṣa protected his subjects righteously for countless years, he fell into a most dreadful old age that destroys beauty.
t.1.70.34: Overcome by old age, that king spoke these words to his sons, Yadu, Pūru, Turvasu, Druhyu, and Anu, O Bhārata.
t.1.70.35: Pursuing my desires through youthfulness, I wish, as a young man, to sport with young women; give me your help, my dear sons.
t.1.70.36: His son Yadu, the firstborn, born of Devayānī, said to him: "What task of yours, sir, is to be done by us with our youth?"
t.1.70.37: Yayāti said to him, "Let my old age be taken on by you; with your youth I would enjoy the pleasures of the senses."
t.1.70.39: Let one of you rule the kingdom with my body, while I, young again with a fresh body, may obtain my desires.
t.1.70.38: While I was occupied with long sacrificial sessions, and through the curse of the sage Uśanas, my aim of pleasure has gone unfulfilled; I am tormented by that, my dear sons.
t.1.70.40: They, Yadu and the others, did not accept his old age. Then Pūru, the youngest, whose valor was true, spoke to him.
t.1.70.41: O king, roam about with a fresh body, abiding in the realm of youth; I, taking on your old age, shall remain in the kingdom at your command.
t.1.70.42: Thus addressed, that royal seer, by resorting to the power of his austerities, then transferred his old age to his great-souled son.
t.1.70.43: Then the king, with Pūru's age, attained youth; and Pūru, with Yayāti's age, carried on the rule of the kingdom.
t.1.70.44: Then, at the end of a thousand years, the unconquered Yayāti, still unsated with his desires, spoke to his son Pūru.
t.1.70.45: Through you I have an heir; you are my son, the founder of my lineage. Your lineage will attain fame in the world as the Paurava line.
t.1.70.46: Then that tiger among kings, having consecrated Pūru in the kingship, afterwards, after a long time, met the law of time.
